title: Synthetic Data in Healthcare and Drug Development: Definitions, Regulatory Frameworks, Issues

content.abstract_summary: Critical narrative review distinguishing observed external controls from artificial data generated by process-driven or data-driven methods. It proposes clearer terminology and emphasizes provenance, transparency, validation, and the absence of a harmonized regulatory pathway for AI-generated synthetic data in drug approval.
key_findings: The PubMed search covered 1986-2025, returned 208 results, and retained 91 relevant instances.
The paper distinguishes observed data, RWD, fully/partially/hybrid synthetic data, external control arms, process-driven synthetic data, and data-driven synthetic data.
Process-driven simulation such as PBPK, PopPK/PD, and QSP has established use in drug development, whereas data-driven AI-generated synthetic data remains less established regulatorily.
Synthetic-data provenance should document source data, generation algorithms/models, transformations, and intended use.
Distributional similarity and privacy assumptions should not be treated as automatic evidence of regulatory suitability.
limitations: Critical narrative rather than systematic-review methodology.
Terminology and regulatory frameworks are evolving.
The paper does not empirically compare Claude, Codex, or Antigravity.

extracted_claims.text: Observed external controls and algorithmically generated artificial data should not both be left under an ambiguous synthetic-data label.
Robust provenance requires documentation of source data, generating models, transformations, and methodology.
AI-generated data remain without a harmonized regulatory definition or established drug-approval precedent, unlike process-driven model simulations.

numerical_findings.description: PubMed records returned by the review search

gaps_addressed: Supports explicit terminology, provenance, disclosure, and context-of-use scoring in M4.2, M4.5-A10, and M4.5-A11.

provenance.notes: Open full text reviewed through PMC, focusing on methodology, terminology, provenance, regulatory discussion, and conclusions.
